ucs.title: [LLM] Qilin / Agenda — Chrome credential harvesting via GPO logon-script (IPScanner.ps1)
ucs.description: Hunts Qilin's distinctive August-2024 tradecraft of pushing a PowerShell harvester (IPScanner.ps1 / IPScanner.txt) through a Group Policy logon script that reads Chrome's Login Data SQLite + Local State key blob from every workstation the affected user logs into. Sophos X-Ops attributed this exact chain (GPO → gpscript.exe → powershell.exe → Chrome SQLite read → SMB share staging) to a Qilin affiliate inside a UK organization in July 2024.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("gpscript.exe","userinit.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Login Data*" OR Processes.process="*Google\\Chrome\\User Data*" OR Processes.process="*Local State*" OR Processes.process="*CryptUnprotectData*" OR Processes.process="*IPScanner*" OR Processes.process="*ProtectedDataDecrypt*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user, "\\$$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("gpscript.exe","userinit.exe")     // GPO logon-script execution context
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"Google\Chrome\User Data", "Login Data", "Local State", "CryptUnprotectData", "ProtectedDataDecrypt", "IPScanner")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)System\.Data\.SQLite|Microsoft\.Win32\.SafeHandles|os_crypt"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"                                            // exclude machine accounts
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          PsCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          PsHash   = SHA256, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\gpscript.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\userinit.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"Google\Chrome\User Data", "Login Data", "Local State", "CryptUnprotectData", "IPScanner", "ProtectedDataDecrypt")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Qilin Ransomware GPO-Deployed Chrome Credential Theft (IPScanner.ps1)
id: 8c3f9d12-a4b7-4e15-9c8f-d7e02b41a930
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell launched from a Group Policy logon-script context (gpscript.exe / userinit.exe) that reads Chrome credential stores or matches the Qilin IPScanner.ps1 harvester pattern documented by Sophos X-Ops (Aug 2024).
references:
  - https://news.sophos.com/en-us/2024/08/22/qilin-ransomware-caught-stealing-credentials-stored-in-google-chrome/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1037.001
  - attack.t1059.001
  - threatgroup.qilin
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\gpscript.exe'
      - '\userinit.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Login Data'
      - 'Google\Chrome\User Data'
      - 'Local State'
      - 'CryptUnprotectData'
      - 'ProtectedDataDecrypt'
      - 'IPScanner'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_parent and selection_cmd and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned password-migration scripts pushed by IT via GPO (rare, should be allow-listed by script hash)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\gpscript.exe OR *\GPScript.exe OR *\userinit.exe OR *\Userinit.exe OR *\USERINIT.EXE) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\Pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*"Login Data"* OR *"Google\\Chrome\\User Data"* OR *"Local State"* OR *CryptUnprotectData* OR *ProtectedDataDecrypt* OR *IPScanner*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/(gpscript|userinit)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(Login\\s+Data|Google\\\\Chrome\\\\User\\s+Data|Local\\s+State|CryptUnprotectData|ProtectedDataDecrypt|IPScanner|os_crypt)", field=CommandLine)
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ucs.rationale: GPO logon scripts that fork PowerShell are themselves rare; ones that read Chrome's Login Data SQLite + Local State key blob in the same process are essentially never benign. Sophos X-Ops attributed this exact gpscript.exe → powershell.exe → Chrome SQLite read chain to a Qilin affiliate in the only publicly disclosed Qilin engagement where the harvester was recovered. Pivoting on parent=gpscript.e

ucs.title: [LLM] Qilin / Agenda — Safe-Mode reboot + shadow-copy destruction chain pre-encryption
ucs.description: Hunts the Qilin/Agenda pre-encryption ritual: bcdedit /set {default} safeboot (minimal|network) to reboot the host into Safe Mode and bypass EDR drivers, paired within ~30 minutes with vssadmin/wbadmin/wmic shadow-copy destruction on the same host. Trend Micro and Group-IB have documented this combination in multiple Agenda Rust-variant deployments since 2023; the safeboot + recovery-destruction co-occurrence is the strongest pre-encryption signature for this family.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="bcdedit.exe" AND Processes.process="*safeboot*") OR (Processes.process_name="vssadmin.exe" AND Processes.process="*delete*" AND Processes.process="*shadows*") OR (Processes.process_name="wbadmin.exe" AND (Processes.process="*delete catalog*" OR Processes.process="*delete systemstatebackup*")) OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*shadowcopy*" AND Processes.process="*delete*") by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval is_safeboot=if(match(cmds,"(?i)safeboot"),1,0), is_recovery=if(match(cmds,"(?i)(delete shadows|delete catalog|shadowcopy delete|delete systemstatebackup)"),1,0) | stats sum(is_safeboot) as safeboot_hits sum(is_recovery) as recovery_hits values(cmds) as cmds values(procs) as procs by dest user | where safeboot_hits>0 AND recovery_hits>0
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let WindowMinutes = 30;
let SafeBoot = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "safeboot"           // covers /set {default} safeboot minimal|network
    | project SafeBootTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SafeBootUser = AccountName, SafeBootCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
let Recovery = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("delete","shadows"))
         or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe"  and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("delete catalog","delete systemstatebackup"))
         or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe"     and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy","delete"))
    | project RecoveryTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, RecoveryFile = FileName, RecoveryCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
SafeBoot
| join kind=inner Recovery on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', SafeBootTime, RecoveryTime)) <= WindowMinutes
| project SafeBootTime, RecoveryTime,
          DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', RecoveryTime, SafeBootTime),
          DeviceName, SafeBootUser, SafeBootCmd, RecoveryFile, RecoveryCmd
| order by SafeBootTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let WindowMinutes = 30;
let SafeBoot = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\bcdedit.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "safeboot"
    | project SafeBootTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SafeBootUser = SubjectUserName, SafeBootCmd = CommandLine;
let Recovery = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has_all ("delete","shadows"))
         or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wbadmin.exe"  and CommandLine has_any ("delete catalog","delete systemstatebackup"))
         or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe"     and CommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy","delete"))
    | project RecoveryTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, RecoveryProc = NewProcessName, RecoveryCmd = CommandLine;
SafeBoot
| join kind=inner Recovery on Computer
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', SafeBootTime, RecoveryTime)) <= WindowMinutes
| project SafeBootTime, RecoveryTime,
          DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', RecoveryTime, SafeBootTime),
          Computer, SafeBootUser, SafeBootCmd, RecoveryProc, RecoveryCmd
| order by SafeBootTime desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Qilin / Agenda Ransomware Safe-Mode Boot Configuration
id: 1a2d4f87-6c93-4b08-9f1c-3e5b7a02d614
status: experimental
description: Detects bcdedit being used to configure the host to boot into Safe Mode — Qilin/Agenda (and a small number of other ransomware families e.g. Snatch, BlackBasta) reboot endpoints into Safe Mode to evade EDR drivers immediately before triggering encryption.
references:
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/22/l/agenda-ransomware-uses-rust-to-target-more-vital-industries.html
  - https://www.group-ib.com/blog/qilin-ransomware/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1562.009
  - attack.t1490
  - threatgroup.qilin
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'safeboot minimal'
      - 'safeboot network'
      - '/set {default} safeboot'
      - '/set {current} safeboot'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate sysadmin Safe Mode troubleshooting (rare on production servers; should be allow-listed by host/user)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEDIT.EXE OR *\BCDEdit.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*safeboot* OR *SAFEBOOT* OR *SafeBoot*)) OR (@Image:(*\vssadmin.exe OR *\VSSADMIN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*"delete shadows"* OR *"Delete Shadows"* OR *"DELETE SHADOWS"*)) OR (@Image:(*\wbadmin.exe OR *\WBADMIN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*"delete catalog"* OR *"delete systemstatebackup"*)) OR (@Image:(*\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*"shadowcopy delete"* OR *"ShadowCopy Delete"*))
ucs.rationale: bcdedit safeboot is rare on production endpoints to begin with (almost no benign automation reconfigures the boot loader to Safe Mode). Demanding it co-occur within 30 minutes of shadow-copy destruction on the same host shrinks the result set to effectively only ransomware pre-encryption activity, and within that set Qilin/Agenda is the dominant active 2024-2026 RaaS using this exact ritual on Win
